title: "Working With tidycensus"

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  eval = identical(Sys.getenv("IN_PKGDOWN"), "true") &&
    nzchar(Sys.getenv("CENSUS_API_KEY"))
)
```

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(griddy)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
```

This article runs the core `griddy` workflow on census tracts in San
Francisco, using median household income (ACS table B19013) from three
five-year American Community Survey samples: 2008–2012, 2013–2017, and
2018–2022. The samples do not overlap, so each tract contributes two
transitions. The article needs a Census API key. It renders on the pkgdown
site when one is set and does not ship with the package.

```{r, results='hide', fig.alt=c("Heatmap of ACS tract transition probabilities between income quintiles.", "Faceted heatmaps of ACS tract spatial Markov transition probabilities by spatial-lag quintile.", "Map of ACS tract endpoint rank mobility.")}
library(tidycensus)
library(sf)
library(sfdep)

years <- c(2012, 2017, 2022)

acs <- purrr::map_dfr(years, function(y) {
  get_acs(
    geography = "tract",
    variables = "B19013_001",
    state = "CA",
    county = "San Francisco",
    year = y,
    survey = "acs5",
    geometry = TRUE
  ) |>
    transmute(
      GEOID,
      year = y,
      median_income = estimate,
      geometry
    ) |>
    filter(is.finite(median_income))
})

geography <- acs |>
  filter(year == max(year)) |>
  filter(!st_is_empty(geometry)) |>
  arrange(GEOID)

common_ids <- acs |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  count(GEOID) |>
  filter(n == length(years)) |>
  pull(GEOID) |>
  intersect(geography$GEOID)

panel <- acs |>
  filter(GEOID %in% common_ids) |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  left_join(select(geography, GEOID, geometry), by = "GEOID") |>
  st_as_sf()

geography <- geography |>
  filter(GEOID %in% common_ids) |>
  arrange(GEOID) |>
  mutate(
    nb = st_contiguity(geometry, queen = TRUE),
    wt = st_weights(nb, allow_zero = TRUE)
  )

classes <- classify_dynamics(panel, GEOID, year, median_income, k = 5)
classic <- markov_dynamics(classes, GEOID, year, class)
spatial <- spatial_markov(panel, GEOID, year, median_income, geometry = geography, k = 5)
mobility <- rank_mobility(panel, GEOID, year, median_income)

plot_transition_matrix(classic)
plot_spatial_markov(spatial)
plot_rank_mobility(mobility)
```

## Reading the output

The first plot is the classic transition matrix: the probability that a tract
in one income class is in each class five years later, pooled over both steps.
The second splits the same transitions by the income class of each tract's
neighbors at the start of the step. The map shows each tract's change in
income rank between the first and last samples.

## Before using this for analysis

Two simplifications keep the example short.

- **Incomes are not comparable across samples.** Each sample reports income
  in dollars of its own final year. With pooled breaks, inflation and
  citywide growth move most tracts into higher classes, so the matrix mixes
  shared growth with relative movement. To study relative movement, divide
  each sample's incomes by their median before classifying.
  [Get Started](griddy.html) does the same with state incomes and the
  national mean.
- **Tract boundaries changed in 2020.** The 2008–2012 and 2013–2017 samples
  use 2010 tracts, and the 2018–2022 sample uses 2020 tracts. Matching on
  `GEOID` keeps tracts whose identifier persisted, but a persisting identifier
  does not guarantee an unchanged boundary, and split or merged tracts drop
  out. Interpolate the earlier samples to 2020 tracts first, for example with
  `tidycensus::interpolate_pw()`.
